newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Koor says it keeping to strategic plan.
newsitem.headline: Koor says it keeping to strategic plan.

text.p: Israel's Koor Industries will continue to operate according to its five-year strategic plan to expand operations despite its chairman's proposal to spin off key businesses, the company said on Monday.

"The company's board of directors have not discussed the subject of a break-up and if this matter were to be brought up and decisions taken to change the strategic plan, shareholders will be informed and management will act according to those decisions," Koor said in a statement to the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

The statement came four days after Koor's chairman Stanley Gold said he wanted to spin off many of Koor's biggest publicly traded holdings to shareholders. Gold is also president of Koor's second-biggest shareholder, California-based Shamrock Holdings Ltd.

In March, Koor's directors approved a five-year strategic programme to focus and expand the company's three core activities -- telecommunications and electronics, agro-chemicals and building materials.
The programme called for boosting group revenues for Israel's biggest holding company to $5 billion by the year 2000, half of them from exports. Koor's revenues last year were $3.5 billion.
Koor noted in Monday's statement that the five-year programme called for divesting or reducing stakes in "non-synergistic" businesses.

But Gold's plan would strip Koor of key holdings in its basic businesses, including electronics company Tadiran Ltd, agro-chemicals maker Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd and its Agan Chemicals Manufacturers Ltd unit.
A Koor spokesman said the company had in the meantime set up a team of outside consultants to study the tax, legal and financial implications of the possible spin-offs.
